signals.title: danishhraza/atrium-agent-orchestration
signals.content: Build your own team of AI agents: an orchestrator that delegates, agents that hand off and consult each other, per-agent RAG, learned model routing, and a live clubhouse UI.
signals.score_reason: high-value open-source ecosystem signal; agentic AI relevance; retrieval/RAG relevance; model capability relevance. Final score: 81. Freshness: source age 0d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: danishhraza/atrium-agent-orchestration

Brief: This open‑source framework enables the construction of a modular AI team. An orchestrator component assigns tasks to specialized agents, which can delegate further, consult peers, and perform per‑agent retrieval‑augmented generation (RAG). The system supports learned routing models to select the most suitable agent for a given query and includes a real‑time web UI (Clubhouse) for monitoring and interaction. Current implementations are experimental; performance and security depend on the underlying models and integration choices.

signals.content: 🚨 Full circle. China, Russia, American technology, taxpayer investment, and now Google seeking even more computing capacity from SpaceX. Remember Google's history. 2017: Google establishes an AI research presence in China. 2018: Google decides not to renew its Pentagon Project Maven AI contract after employee protests. 2018: Google is also developing Project Dragonfly, a proposed censored search engine for China. 2019: General Joseph Dunford, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, warns Congress that Google's work in China could benefit the Chinese military. Google subsequently ends Dragonfly, but the questions about American technology and national security remain. Now follow SpaceX. 1993–1996: American taxpayers support the experimental DC-X reusable rocket program. 1997: Boeing and McDonnell Douglas merge. 2001–2002: Elon Musk travels to Russia seeking rockets. 2006: NASA awards SpaceX a $278 million development agreement. 2019: Tesla begins manufacturing in Shanghai. 2025: Vladimir Putin publicly praises Elon Musk. 2026: Reuters reports Google wants more SpaceX computing capacity. American innovation. American taxpayer support. American national-security interests. Who controls the infrastructure? What technology protections exist? Who benefits financially? What safeguards prevent foreign military access? These records do not prove technology theft or espionage. They establish why public oversight matters. Greed knows no color only money and power. 🇺🇸 Our nation's technology, merit, treasure and sacrifices deserve accountability across both political parties. signals.brief_en: Brief: Recent UN discussions in Geneva highlighted growing concerns over autonomous weapon systems (AWS). While participants agreed to draft non‑binding guidelines, they failed to secure a binding treaty. Current evidence suggests some AI‑driven weapons can select targets within limited parameters, but full autonomous decision‑making remains unproven. signals.title: @chenYijl: Three agencies. One week. Zero answers. On November 24, the Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network said someone got inside its syst
signals.content: Three agencies. One week. Zero answers. On November 24, the Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network said someone got inside its systems. FinCEN is the office that collects the suspicious-activity reports banks file on Americans. It took some systems offline and pushed filing deadlines back to December 30. Reports due between November 18 and December 29 now have until the end of the year. FinCEN has not said who got in, how long they stayed, or what they saw. It did say one thing that matters. Investigators currently see no evidence the Bank Secrecy Act database or the beneficial-ownership registers were breached. That is the database part. The rest is still unknown. The same day, the New York Times reported a separate breach: an unclassified intelligence-analysis system used by the CIA, the Director of National Intelligence and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency. An AP source said no classified information was involved, and the issue was resolved. Unnamed sources told the Times the attackers may have used ARTEX, an AI hacking framework. The FBI had warned about ARTEX on November 13. Its advisory said the tool lets attackers with limited technical skill run multi-target intrusions at machine speed. Early indications point to China, two people told the Times. Neither the CIA nor the FBI has confirmed that. The Director of National Intelligence said the week's outages were not coordinated and not state-sponsored. And the FBI's own crime database was hacked earlier in November. The NCIC break-in was the second attack on FBI systems since September. Meanwhile, researchers at Intruder Systems showed they could take over five Treasury subdomains for $3 each, by claiming the AWS addresses the domains still pointed to. The pattern is not one breach. It is a week of them. The agencies that hold the files on everyone else's money and secrets spent the week locking their own doors after the fact. No evidence the crown jewels were taken. No evidence they were not, either. That gap is the story. If the people who watch the money cannot watch their own network, who watches the watchers?

signals.brief_en: Three agencies, one week, no answers. On 24 Nov, the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed an intrusion into its systems. FinCEN, which aggregates banks’ suspicious‑activity reports (SARs) on U.S. persons, temporarily shut down parts of its platform and extended filing deadlines to 30 Dec. SARs due 18 Nov–29 Dec now have until year‑end. FinCEN did not identify the attacker, duration of access, or data viewed. It confirmed no evidence of compromise to the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) database or the beneficial‑ownership registers, but the scope of the breach remains unclear.
signals.brief_ar: ثلاث وكالات، أسبوع واحد، ولا إجابات. في 24 نوفمبر، أفصَل مكتب إنفاذ الجرائم المالية بوزارة الخزانة (FinCEN) عن اختراق أنظمته. يُجمع FinCEN تقارير النشاط المشبوه (SAR) التي تُقدِّمها البنوك عن الأشخاص الأمريكيين، وقد عطل أجزاءً من منصته مؤقتًا ويمدّد مواعيد تقديم التقارير حتى 30 ديسمبر. الآن تُمنح التقارير المستحقة بين 18 نوفمبر و29 ديسمبر مهلة حتى نهاية العام. لم يُحدِّد FinCEN هوية المتسلل، أو مدة وجوده، أو ما رآه. وأكد عدم وجود دليل على اختراق قاعدة بيانات قانون سرية البنوك أو سجلات الملكية المستفيدة، لكن نطاق الاختراق لا يزال غير واضح.

signals.content: 🚨 Full circle. China, Russia, American technology, taxpayer investment, and now Google paying SpaceX $920 MILLION A MONTH for computing capacity. Remember the timeline. 1997: Boeing and McDonnell Douglas merge. 2001–2002: Elon Musk travels to Russia seeking rockets before founding SpaceX. 2006: NASA awards SpaceX a $278 million development agreement. 2019: Tesla begins manufacturing in Shanghai, China. 2025: Vladimir Putin publicly praises Elon Musk. 2026: Google and Anthropic sign computing agreements with SpaceX worth more than $70 billion combined. Now Google reportedly wants MORE computing power. America's engineering, public investment, national security, and generations of sacrifice helped build the foundation for these opportunities. Yet Washington keeps allowing critical capabilities to become concentrated among a politically connected few, while both party machines take turns claiming they're protecting the American people. Who owns the technology? Who controls the infrastructure? What protections prevent foreign access? What returns do taxpayers receive? Who investigates conflicts of interest? And what happens when America's security becomes another corporation's cost of doing business? Greed knows no color only money and power. 🇺🇸 The American people deserve answers, not another two-party spin cycle.
